## Definition

Assume AC for the string-link quotient branch. Use the closed-link residue
definition one finite maximum index length at a time, so its based word-lift
data are finite.

Let $\tau$ be a based $r$-component string link with $r\geq1$ and bottom meridian symbol group
$F_r=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_r\rangle$, exterior group $G=\pi_1(X_\tau)$, and
based string-link longitudes $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r$. With compatible stem accesses this free group identifies the full endpoint fundamental group. For arbitrary independently based meridians, use instead its meridian map on each finite nilpotent quotient, which is still an isomorphism by the end-identification theorem; no full-group free-basis assertion is made. Longitudes retain their specified parallel and access data. For a multi-index
$I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k,j)$ with $k\geq1$ and each index in $\{1,\ldots,r\}$,
let $w_{j,k}\in F_r/\Gamma_{k+1}F_r$ be the unique class whose image under
the bottom-end nilpotent isomorphism is the class of $\lambda_j$ in
$G/\Gamma_{k+1}G$. Define the integer coefficient
$$\mu_\tau(I)=[X_{i_1}\cdots X_{i_k}]\,E(w_{j,k})\in\mathbb Z,$$
where the bracket means the coefficient of that word in the finite Magnus
expansion through degree $k$. The commutator-degree lemma makes this coefficient
independent of the representative of $w_{j,k}$.

For a closed labeled link $L$, choose a common basing and its preferred
zero-self-meridian longitudes. For every component $j$ and every finite
$q\geq2$, choose a lift $w_{j,q}\in F_r/\Gamma_qF_r$ of the class of its
longitude in $G/\Gamma_qG$, where $G=\pi_1(E_L)$ and $F_r$ is free on the
component meridian symbols. Such lifts exist because those meridians generate
every finite nilpotent quotient. For $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k,j)$, define the based
coefficient $\mu_L^b(I)$ by taking the coefficient of
$X_{i_1}\cdots X_{i_k}$ in $E(w_{j,k+1})$ through degree $k$. Let
$\Delta_I^b$ be the nonnegative greatest common divisor of the finite set of
all $\mu_L^b(J)$ for sequences $J$ of lengths from $2$ to $|I|-1$ that occur
as subsequences of cyclic permutations of $I$. The gcd of an empty set is $0$.
Define the based residue candidate
$$\bar\mu_L^b(I):=\mu_L^b(I)\pmod{\Delta_I^b}\in \mathbb Z/\Delta_I^b\mathbb Z,$$
with $\mathbb Z/0\mathbb Z=\mathbb Z$. Independence of the basing and word
lifts is not part of this definition; it is a separate theorem. A based
Borromean example with $I=(1,2,3)$ uses this convention.

actual_named_consumer.peripheral_definition_quote: Choose a basepoint on the outer boundary of $P_-$, a path in the side boundary of $C$ to the corresponding top basepoint, and basing paths from these points to the component meridians. Each end inclusion, with the chosen connecting path for the top end, induces a based homomorphism $\iota_\pm:\pi_1(P_\pm)\to\pi_1(X_\tau)$. For each string component choose a parallel path on its tube boundary from the bottom endpoint to the top endpoint, and choose access paths that close it to a based loop using the fixed side connector. The resulting element of $\pi_1(X_\tau)$ is its based string-link longitude; the parallel and access paths are part of the peripheral datum. The positively oriented boundaries of the endpoint tube disks are the designated meridian loops. Stacking two string links means rescaling them into the lower and upper halves of $C$ and identifying their matching endpoint collars; closure joins each top endpoint to the matching bottom endpoint outside $C$ and retains the component labels.
actual_named_consumer.closed_peripheral_definition_quote: For a nonempty labeled oriented link $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r$ in the oriented three-sphere, choose pairwise disjoint closed product tubes $N(K_i)$, put $E_L=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}\bigl(\bigcup_iN(K_i)\bigr)$, and write $T_i=\partial N(K_i)$. A positive meridian $\mu_i$ is the oriented boundary of a normal disk, with the disk orientation fixed by the rule that the oriented tangent of $K_i$ followed by the disk orientation gives the ambient orientation. A degree-one parallel is a simple closed curve on $T_i$ whose projection to $K_i$ has degree $+1$. A based longitude is the class of such a parallel transported to the common basepoint by a specified path. When the positive meridians form a basis of $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)$, the self-meridian coordinate of a longitude is its coefficient on $[\mu_i]$. A preferred zero-self-meridian longitude is a chosen degree-one parallel whose self-meridian coordinate is zero. The choice, when it exists, is part of the peripheral datum; this definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness. Changing a common basing path conjugates the peripheral group elements simultaneously.
actual_named_consumer.logical_use: The definition receives based string-link longitudes as input, identifies their nilpotent classes using the declared end theorem, and extracts Magnus coefficients. For a closed link it chooses preferred degree-one zero-self-meridian longitudes, uses declared homology/meridian inputs for existence and the declared nilpotent-generation lemma to choose finite word lifts. These are group/peripheral definitions, not diagram computations. It never scans crossings, constructs W_j(D), corrects self-writhe, or uses the explicit access/parallel transport-word formula.
